scenes.say: What makes music a problem for you, beyond distraction?
scenes.sayA: It drives imagination: scenes 2.7 times more vivid, deeper immersion, and harder exits. For 36 of 41 people with MD, music deepened the daydream.
scenes.a: It drives imagination: 2.7× more vivid, deeper, harder to exit

scenes.say: In the loop, what comes right after instant relief?
scenes.sayA: The habit strengthens, so the urge comes faster next time.

scenes.say: Over 13 months, what did MD predict, and what did not predict MD?
scenes.sayA: MD predicted later stress, anxiety and depression. Distress did not predict later MD.
scenes.a: MD → later stress, anxiety, depression. Not the reverse.

scenes.say: Why ask a mentor to walk you through the last time, instead of asking for advice?
scenes.sayA: Because experts leave out about 70 percent of their decisions when they explain how they work.
scenes.a: Experts omit ~70% of their decisions when explaining

scenes.say: What are the four parts of WOOP, and which kind of obstacle do you name?
scenes.sayA: Wish, outcome, obstacle, plan. And you name the inner obstacle.

scenes.head: One thread through everything
scenes.text: Every trap sells the same product: *the feeling of progress* without the progress. Measure progress in ~shipped output~.
scenes.say: Every trap in this video sells the same product: the feeling of progress without the progress. A success fantasy mentally consummates the goal and drains the energy to pursue it. A tutorial makes you feel able without making you able. Unrestricted AI raises practice scores while independent skill falls. And a soundtrack makes the fantasy richer and the exit harder. So measure progress in shipped output: a hook written, an edit rebuilt, a test run.

scenes.text: The moment work gets uncomfortable is *when MD fires*, and also *when skill is built*. Stay ~two more minutes~.
scenes.say: That is why the moment work gets uncomfortable deserves so much attention. It is when MD fires, and it is also when effortful practice builds skill. Learning to stay in that moment for two more minutes protects your focus and builds your craft at the same time.

scenes.text: Not zero imagination. *Cut the rituals*: music, solitude, the bed. Give imagination a ~container~: written, time-boxed, obstacle-aware, ending in action.
scenes.note: Your daily log is the best data you'll get
scenes.say: The goal is not zero imagination. Suppression rebounds, and vivid imagination is a risk factor, not the disease. The realistic goal is to cut the rituals that turn imagination into compulsion: music, solitude and the bed, and to give imagination a container: written, time-boxed, obstacle-aware, and ending in action. Your conviction about music happens to remove the strongest amplifier the research identifies, and change grounded in your own values tends to last. How fast this works for a young man whose daydreaming is tied to work is still an open question. Your daily log is the best data you will get on it.

scenes.head: Start today

scenes.say: Start today with three things. One if-then plan, written and rehearsed. One log entry tonight. And one silent work block tomorrow.
